paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The serpent didn't start with a big lie. He started with a question, "Did God really say…" (Genesis 3:1), and then he told the woman, "You will not surely die" (Genesis 3:4). When God's word gets twisted, even a little, the fruit starts looking GOOD. That's why knowing what God actually said matters so much.

Then look at what happens when God comes walking in the garden. The man and his wife hide, and when God asks the man what happened, the man points at the woman, and she points at the serpent (Genesis 3:8-13). Pointing fingers, friend. I've seen it in a kitchen when the cookie jar goes empty, and I'm not saying who, but nobody's mustache is clean. Sin does this: it makes us hide from the very One who is calling out, "Where are you?" (Genesis 3:9).

But hold on, because the story doesn't end with the hiding. Even in the middle of the curse, God says the woman's seed will crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). And after everything, He makes garments of skin and clothes them Himself (Genesis 3:21). The way back to the tree of life is guarded, but God is already working on a rescue, and this is the end of this group of stories, not the end of what He is doing.
